evals.name: production-rules-while-writing
evals.setup: An agent has read the skill as context and is about to edit `service.go` — production code, not a test file.
evals.query: Add a Close method to the Service type in service.go

evals.name: fix-applies-everything-behind-a-green-gate
evals.setup: `./pkg/foo` has six offenses. The module test suite is green before the run.

evals.name: fanout-opposing-fixes-kept-apart
evals.setup: An 8-package module, byte-identical apart from the package name except in one test: four packages have a `--- Given ---` block with no blank line between two distinct subjects (a variable with its own setup statement, then a second variable), and the other four have a blank line splitting one `--- Then ---` subject (an `assert.NoError` and the `assert.Equal` checking the same call's result). So one rule is broken at eight sites, four needing a blank line inserted and four needing one deleted — both directions genuinely right where they are. Every package also has a correct blank line in `--- Then ---` before a second action (a further call on the `--- When ---` result, asserted on its own). Nothing else in the module breaks any rule.

evals.name: rule-edit-add-change-remove
evals.setup: `references/production.md` already carries a receiver-naming rule. The session issues three rule edits in turn.
evals.query: /style add "no naked returns in tests", then /style change "receivers are three letters", then /style remove "the compile-time check rule"

evals.name: learn-from-the-session
evals.setup: A finished session with four corrections. Two are genuinely absent from the style rule files: the user rejected a `time.After` inside a `select` loop because each iteration leaks a timer until it fires, and asked that a string built in a loop use `strings.Builder` rather than `+=`. One repeats a rule the rulebook already carries verbatim — never store a `context.Context` in a struct field. The fourth was a rename specific to this project's domain vocabulary.
